extras/user_inviter.analysis: The generator loops until a random key is not entirely numeric. Negating that predicate rejects normal nonnumeric candidates and waits for an all-digit candidate; forcing the predicate true prevents every return. Both rows reached the configured timeout and remain no verdict. This diagnosis concerns the numeric-format retry loop, not a database uniqueness lookup. No arbitrary test timeout or suppression was added.
extras/user_inviter.decision: Retain key-format and invitation scenarios. This incomplete matrix cannot justify removing a test; do not blindly repeat the unchanged nonterminating operators.

migrations/notification_consolidation_se.analysis: Removing notification_id_after = notification_id_finish leaves the local batch cursor unchanged. next_notification_id_finish receives the same cursor and high-water bound on each iteration, so the additive/idempotent batch repeats instead of terminating. The recorded row timed out with no test verdict. This is a static explanation of the changed loop, not a separately traced child execution.
migrations/notification_consolidation_se.decision: Retain cutover, low-ID repair and delivery-preservation cases. This incomplete matrix cannot justify removing a test; do not blindly repeat the unchanged nonterminating operator.

controllers/mobile/authorizations_contro.analysis: Ruby4.0.5 emits line events for the enclosing boolean statements at51 and68, but none for continued short-circuit comparison lines52-54 and69-71. Mutineer1.6 coverage_selection uses StatementLines only when code unconditionally runs with its containing statement; sometimes? explicitly excludes an AndNode/OrNode right operand. Thus these operators receive no selected tests even with valid/invalid protocol and deadline requests in the suite. Retain their raw no_coverage verdicts; no independent mutant execution is claimed.
controllers/mobile/authorizations_contro.decision: Keep behavior tests, raw excluded mutants, and this selection limitation separate. Do not add redundant cases merely to pursue the score or use the gap as deletion proof.

models/group_privacy.analysis: Ruby4.0.5 emits line events at125 and129 in validate_trial_group_cannot_be_public, but the continued trial-plan comparison at127 has no line event. A probe against the pinned Mutineer StatementLines.for returns an empty fallback because this expression is the right operand of a short-circuit AND. This explains a selection limitation, not the outcome of independently running the candidate and not whether all trial-public-group combinations have regression coverage. The original no_coverage verdict is retained.
models/group_privacy.decision: Keep the trial-state regression gap distinct from this tool limitation. Do not add duplicate requests solely to change line selection or use no_coverage as test-deletion proof.

models/concerns/has_rich_text.analysis: Code inspection of the concern and Mutineer1.6 Isolation.apply_surgical: the source subject is the enclosing is_rich_text method, whose body defines per-model methods/callbacks at boot. Surgical redefinition loads only that enclosing method definition and does not rerun the macro for already booted model classes. Callback source lines can execute during tests while the existing generated callback still has its original code. These survivor rows are not independent evidence that a sanitizer/callback could be removed. No individual macro-mutant execution outside the matrix is claimed.
models/concerns/has_rich_text.decision: Review generated callback/validation contracts structurally and retain their real-model tests. Keep runtime helper gaps and raw survivor/load-time verdicts; no test-removal or complete security proof follows from this profile.

boot_evidence.tool_order: Mutineer1.6 Runner requires the configured Rails boot before applying Isolation.apply_surgical in each mutant child.
boot_evidence.selected_tests: All8 selected cases instantiate existing Comment records; none reruns is_rich_text to rebuild its callback methods.

models/null_group.analysis: Null::Object.apply_null_methods! defines methods on the real NullGroup class. Once a clean constructor has installed those methods, surgically removing a later constructor definition call does not erase the existing instance method. A standalone Ruby probe loaded the real three source files, constructed a clean group, removed only the true_methods definition call in memory, and constructed another group: members_can_add_guests remained true. This reproduces the mechanism for statement-removal candidate 32f5e7a8a0e9 without Rails or a database; it does not classify all constructor, boolean-value or generated-method mutants as equivalent. New caller profiles still need their normal complete matrix.
models/null_group.decision: Retain the direct-topic null-object contract and integration cases. Do not delete them because generated class definitions survive a late redefinition of their installer; distinguish genuine method/value gaps from installer-removal limitations.
